These appeals coming on for Orders this day,
N.K. Patil, J., delivered the following:
 JUDGMENT

These two appeals are by the wife, being aggrieved by the impugned Judgment and Decree dated 29.11.2010 passed in M.C.No.387/2009 on the file of the II Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bangalore and Judgment and Decree dated 28.10.2013 passed in M.C.No.4375/2011 on the file of the II Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bangalore, respectively.

sentences.text: 2. We have heard the learned Counsel for the appellant and the learned Counsel for the respondent.

3. During the course of the submission, learned counsel appearing for both the parties have filed a compromise petition dated 22.01.2016 duly signed by the appellant and the respondent and attested by their respective counsel.
Further, they submitted that the appeals filed by the appellant may be disposed of in terms of the compromise petition dated 22.01.2016 in the interest of justice and equity.
4. The appellant and the respondent are present before the court.
Their presence is placed on record.
5. Submission made by the learned counsel for both the parties is placed on record.

6. The terms and conditions of the compromise petition dated 22.01.2016 read thus:
"1. The respondent herein is the husband of the appellant, dispute arose between the couples the respondent had filed petition for restitution of conjugal rights before the Family Court Bangalore in M.C.No.387/2009 and the said petition was came to be allowed in favour of the husband on 29.11.2010 and the appellant wife filed appeal against said order before this Hon'ble Court in M.F.A.No.881/2011.

During the pendency of the said appeal the husband respondent herein filed petition for divorce Under Section XIII(1- A) (II) of the Hindu Marriage Act in M.C.No.4375/2011 and the said Petition also decided in favour of the respondent on 28.10.2013 against which the appellant wife filed appeal before this Hon'ble Court in M.F.A No.10214/2013 and both the appeals are pending consideration.

2. During the course of the hearing of the appeals at the intervention of the friends,
well wishers and the elders of the family now the parties are agreed to settle the matter amicably and to live together in considering their future and children of them Smt Rekha vs Sri D Suresh on 22 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74024937/
2 on the following terms:
A) The Appellant agreed to join the company of the respondent husband immediately a week after the completion of the SSLC Examination of their children Kumari.Bhavya and Bharath in the year 2017, who are now studying in 9th standard at Gokul Vidya Kendra, Sarakki, JP Nagar.
Since the children are with the custody of the appellant wife and residing nearby the school which the children are studying in 9th standard.
The respondent husband agreed for the same.

B) After completion of the SSLC examination of the children the respondent agreed to join the company of her husband along with children Bhavya and Bharath, in the event the appellant wife failed to join the company of the husband along with the children immediately a week after the SSLC Examination in the year 2017, the Respondent Husband is at liberty to take the Children Bhavya and Bharath to his custody and looking after them by providing education, food, clothes and other daily Needs.

C) The Respondent husband agreed to pay the maintenance as ordered by the Family Court at Bangalore C.Misc.No.152/2010 till the completion of the SSLC Examination of the Children in the year 2017, further the respondent husband agreed to pay the academic education expenses till the respondent took the children into his custody and also agreed to pay the arrears of maintenance from the month of July, 2015 to end of December 2015 a sum of Rs,12000/- (Rupees Twelve Thousand) @
Rs.2,000/-P.M, the education expenses for SSLC would be paid by the respondent subject to production of relevant bills.

D) The respondent husband undertakes that he will look after the safety and welfare of the appellant/Wife and children, further he undertakes and ensure that there shall not be any harassment, cruelty and life threats to the appellant and children in the matrimonial home after she joining the husband and further the respondent undertakes that he will not dispose of the family properties standing in the name of his Mother without permission of the Court.
E) The respondent is at liberty to visit the children at the residence of the Appellant/Wife whenever he wants and wishes to see them and the petitioner will cooperate in this regard.
F) Both the parties agree that they will withdraw all the petitions, cases if any pending against each other in any Courts.

Wherefore both the appellant and respondent jointly pray that this Hon'ble court be pleased to record the compromise entered into between the parties and pass appropriate order in the interest of justice and equity".
Smt Rekha vs Sri D Suresh on 22 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74024937/
